name: MyFitnessPal API
tagline: Partner-only REST API for user food/exercise diaries—closed to new applicants.
description: MyFitnessPal’s partner-facing REST API (v2) lets approved apps read and write a consenting user’s food and exercise diary, water, body measurements, and profile, with OAuth 2.0 user authorization and optional webhook subscriptions. Official docs and api.myfitnesspal.com remain online, but the developer portal states access is private and the portal home page currently says new API access requests are not being accepted. There is no self-serve signup or published public pricing.

auth.details: Partner-issued OAuth 2.0 client_id + client_secret (no self-serve). Authorization-code grant; API calls use Authorization: Bearer <access_token> plus mfp-client-id (and typically mfp-user-id). OAuth host noted in FAQ: oauth2-api.myfitnesspal.com with Api-Key header = client ID. New access closed as of 2026.

pricing.free_tier_limits: no free tier; partner-only and new access requests not accepted
pricing.paid_plans: not published publicly; contact partners@myfitnesspal.com / API@myfitnesspal.com for enterprise/partner terms

rate_limits: Standard partner accounts: 25,000 requests/day and 60 requests/second (official FAQ); higher limits by request

example.request: curl -s 'https://api.myfitnesspal.com/v2/diary?entry_date=2024-08-25&types=diary_meal,exercise&fields[]=nutritional_contents&fields[]=exercise&fields[]=energy' -H 'Accept: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN' -H 'mfp-client-id: YOUR_CLIENT_ID' -H 'mfp-user-id: YOUR_USER_ID'

use_cases: fetch a user's food diary meals and nutrition totals for a date
log exercise or meal entries into a connected user's diary
read water intake for a given diary date
sync body measurements and profile after OAuth consent
subscribe partners to diary change notifications (webhooks)
